title: Type Promotion in NumPy Operations
keywords: data types, casting, and type promotion
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of type promotion in numpy operations and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply combining different numeric types to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for type promotion in numpy operations.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 62 of the supplied curriculum: **Type Promotion in NumPy Operations**. The main starting point is **Combining different numeric types**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: A dtype controls range, precision, storage, and which operations are valid. Casting should be explicit when loss, overflow, or NumPy 2.x promotion behavior matters.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Type Promotion in NumPy Operations** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Combining different numeric types** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

print(np.result_type(np.int16, np.float32))
print(np.promote_types(np.int16, np.float32))
content_blocks.expected_output:
Observed output in the available validation environment (Python 3.13.5, NumPy 2.3.5):
float32
float32

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: NumPy 2.x follows a revised type-promotion model. Inspect `np.result_type` and test mixed Python/NumPy scalar expressions when migrating older code.

common_mistakes.why: Float-to-integer conversion truncates and narrower dtypes may overflow.
common_mistakes.fix: Check input ranges and precision requirements before casting.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming mixed types promote the same way in every version
common_mistakes.why: NumPy 2.x promotion semantics differ from some older code.
common_mistakes.fix: Test mixed-type operations and consult the migration guide.
